tests_table.Test Description: Validate default reset values and masked read/write behavior across the GPIO control/status registers using per-register read and write masks; confirm readback matches expected values derived from write data and defaults when non-writable bits are preserved.
tests_table.Remarks: Certain registers are intentionally skipped for write/read checks and/or reset-value checks per skip arrays; a note in the source warns that default DIN may read as 1 without external forcing, which can affect reset-value matching.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: invoke the test case entry which first performs a reset-value sweep, then executes masked write/read verification, and finally determines pass/fail based on accumulated mismatch counters.

Reset-value sweep (i = 0..48): for each per-pin/group register (GPIO_8..GPIO_39 and related group/status registers), skip if marked to skip reset check; skip if the read mask is 0; perform a READ of the register, apply a mask to ignore the least significant bit, and compare against the documented default for that register.
Reset-value evaluation: increment a reset-mismatch counter whenever the masked READ value does not equal the documented default.
Prepare write patterns: define six data patterns and iterate over each pattern for the masked write/read checks.

Masked write phase (for each pattern, for each register): if the register is in the skip list, continue; if the write mask is 0, continue; otherwise, perform a WRITE of (pattern AND the register’s write mask) to the target register.

Masked read/compare phase (for each pattern, for each register): skip if not writable or not readable by mask; perform a READ and apply the register’s read mask; compute the expected value by combining the written masked bits with the preserved default bits where the write mask is 0; compare READ vs expected and log a mismatch if different.
Finalization: declare PASS if both the reset-mismatch and write-read mismatch counters remain zero; otherwise declare FAIL.

Validation / Acceptance Criteria: For each register included in the reset sweep, the masked READ value equals the documented default value.
For each pattern and register included in the masked write/read loop, the masked READ value equals the expected combination of written masked bits and preserved default bits.

tests_table.Hidden_Test_Description: Checks default values of registers in addr_array and verifies masked write/read behavior using write_mask_array and read_mask_array. Uses chk_rst_val() then chk_rd_wr(); declares finish(0) if def_fail_cnt==0 and wr_fail_cnt==0 else finish(1).
tests_table.Hidden_Remarks: skip_array and skip_rst_array control which addresses are excluded. Comment states: "when reading default values the din value is becoming 1 automatically if we don't force any value,but if we force zero to din bit level sel becoming high,so that reding value not matched with expected value". Also comment: "SKIPPING VRRW registers".
Hidden_Test_Steps_Procedure: Entry point: int test_case() calls chk_rst_val(); then chk_rd_wr(); finally if(def_fail_cnt>0 || wr_fail_cnt>0) finish(1) else finish(0).

Write loop: for(i=0;i<CNT;i++){ addr=addr_array[i]; if(skip_array[i]==1) continue; if(write_mask_array[i]==0x00000000) continue; else write_reg(addr,(data_wr & write_mask_array[i])); }

Read/compare loop: for(i=0;i<CNT;i++){ addr=addr_array[i]; if(skip_array[i]==1) continue; if(write_mask_array[i]==0x00000000) continue; if(read_mask_array[i]==0x00000000) continue; data_rd = (read_reg(addr) & read_mask_array[i]); wr_n = (write_mask_array[i] ^ 0xffffffff); exp_val = ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | (wr_n & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i])); if(data_rd == exp_val) { /*pass*/ } else { wr_fail_cnt++; printf failure; } }

tests_table.Feature: interrupts can be generated based on positive edge or negative edge or level high or level low detection at GPIO input
tests_table.Test Description: Configure all per-pin control registers to input with negative-edge detection and clear raw status; enable group interrupt for one pin at a time, generate a falling edge per pin, wait with timeout, and in the interrupt service confirm input is low, raw and group statuses set and then cleared, and system interrupt status cleared.
tests_table.Remarks: The wait flag is armed before edge generation to avoid race; a bounded timeout is used during polling to prevent infinite wait.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: enable the appropriate interrupt line in the interrupt controller and the system-interrupt output for the selected GPIO instance via INTR_EN1.
Initialize the external driver register to drive all pads high to establish a known idle level.
For each per-pin control register (GPIO_8..GPIO_39): configure input mode, enable negative-edge detection, and request raw status clear; include a short wait after each configuration write.
For each pin index 0..31: clear the corresponding group raw status bit via GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, enable only the target pin in GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, and briefly wait.
Arm the wait flag before stimulus, then create a falling transition on the targeted pad using the external driver register (drive all high, brief wait, then drive the target bit low).
Poll with a finite timeout for the interrupt flag to be cleared by the service routine; declare a timeout error if the flag remains set after the timeout expires.

In the interrupt service: return the external driver to all-high, read the current pin’s per-pin control register to sample input and raw status bits; check that the input bit reflects low following a falling edge.

Still in service: read GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 to confirm the group status bit corresponding to the pin is set; then clear per-pin raw by writing iclr in the per-pin control register and also clear the group raw bit via GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1.
Verify that GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 reads back as zero after clears; clear the system raw status via RAW_STCR1 and clear the platform interrupt in the interrupt controller.
tests_table.Impacted Registers: INTR_EN1, GPIO_8, GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1, RAW_STCR1
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: No timeout occurs while waiting for each generated falling edge event.
Upon service, the per-pin sampled input bit indicates low following the falling edge.
The group status shows the corresponding bit set during service, and reads back zero after per-pin and group raw clears.
The system raw status is cleared and the platform interrupt is acknowledged.
Overall PASS when no error increments occur; otherwise FAIL.

tests_table.Test Description: Enable positive-edge detection for all pads, set group I/O mode to input, enable group interrupts, generate a rising edge per pad, wait with timeout, and in the interrupt service verify group interrupt is raised, clear all per-pin raw statuses, confirm group status clears, clear system raw status, and re-enable the group interrupt.
tests_table.Remarks: The wait flag is armed before generating the edge; group interrupt is masked during service to avoid re-entry; bounded wait avoids infinite loop.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: enable the GPIO interrupt line in the interrupt controller and enable the GPIO instance output in the system interrupt block via INTR_EN1.
For each per-pin control register (GPIO_8..GPIO_39): configure positive-edge detection.
Set I/O mode to input for all groups using GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1..4 and include short waits.
Enable all pin interrupts via GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1.
For each pad index 0..31: drive the external register low, briefly wait, arm the wait flag, then drive high to create a single rising edge.
Wait for the service to clear the flag with a finite timeout; on timeout record an error and break.
Optionally drive low again and wait briefly to prepare for the next iteration.

In the interrupt service: compute current bit mask from the loop index; clear the pending flag; read GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 and mask group interrupts by writing zero to GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 during service.
If group status indicates an interrupt, proceed; otherwise record an error.
Clear raw per-pin status by writing the clear bit in each per-pin control register (GPIO_8..GPIO_39), then verify that GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 reads zero.
Clear the system raw status via RAW_STCR1 and verify it is cleared; finally re-enable GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 and clear the platform interrupt.

Validation / Acceptance Criteria: No timeout occurs while waiting for each generated rising edge event.
During service, the group masked status indicates an interrupt occurred; after clearing per-pin raw statuses for all pads, the group masked status reads zero.
The system raw status is cleared after issuing the clear and does not remain set.
Overall PASS when no error increments occur; otherwise FAIL.
